title: Review of c09's pcell death-acquired finding: on independent seeds 5 and 6 dying cells start near the median at birth (0.41, 0.53) and erode to 0.03-0.04 by death, splitters start high (0.62, 0.71), marker flat (Supported)
summary: Read table.txt, then ran c09's lifesel.py and lifesel_split.py on my own pcell-multilevel genealogies for seeds 5 and 6 (T=100000, from my review 20261025T0833-c03-review-pcell-multilevel; gen_s5/gen_s6.json.gz there; labkit re-run of the world on seed 5 in rerun/seed5). Dying mature cells (>= 20 snapshots): yield percentile at birth 0.405 and 0.526, mid-life 0.25 and 0.33, 80% of life 0.18 and 0.24, last snapshot 0.026 and 0.044 (39 and 24 cells), while their particle count falls from a median 155-210 to 27-31. Splitting cells: 0.62 and 0.71 at birth. Marker of the dying cells at birth 0.48 and 0.48 (it drifts up to 0.69 on seed 5 by death, down to 0.42 on seed 6). So most of the dying cells' low yield is acquired in their own lifetime, and the inherited part is the birth gap between dying and splitting cells (0.41-0.53 vs 0.62-0.71), as the finding says. This also qualifies my earlier lagged readout (0.14-0.22 at 5000 t before death): the erosion runs over the whole life, not just at the end.

observations.H: lifesel_seeds5_6.txt: dying-cell yield percentile birth 0.405/0.526 -> last 0.026/0.044; splitting cells at birth 0.62/0.71; marker at birth 0.48/0.48

controls_run.H: inert marker zm read the same way (lifesel_seeds5_6.txt)

verdicts.limitation: Percentiles are among cells alive at the same time; the life fractions use snapshots every 50 steps, so short-lived cells (< 20 snapshots) are excluded as in the finding.
